title: Reduce complete first P104 fold time by 29.94% (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Accelerate the complete first P104 shadow-relay fold from PR6170 while preserving its complete output word and acceptance decisions. This is an empirical tooling improvement with a scoped solver-equivalence proof, not a new kappa or supplier audit.

```diff
 solve(A, b)
-  reduce every row above and below each pivot
+  eliminate below each pivot
+  substitute backwards with the same pivot columns and zero free variables
```

The output word and fold construction remain DreamingOfClouds' work. Standard Gaussian elimination is background. This contribution adds the measured solver integration and its reproducible equivalence evidence.

## Evidence

[Proof and package](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/tree/9a7f206d4e9812d2eec042aed6e40acadacd534d/research/p104-fold-elimination).

Median complete-fold time falls from **127.86 s to 89.58 s, a 29.94% reduction**, across five alternating pairs. Baseline range is 123.44 to 132.11 s; candidate range is 86.47 to 91.41 s, on the recorded shared macOS host. All ten commands succeed with zero output differences.

The generated BENCHMARK.json supplies five alternating complete-command pairs, including source authentication, both tried variants, unchanged checks and output serialization. Every run must emit the same canonical 22821-event word and FOLDED report. PROFILE.json puts 75.6 of 83.3 discovery-profile seconds in the original solver; that untimed rejected-variant profile is separate from the benchmark.

Exact reproduction from the repository root, CPython 3.12 and NumPy 2.5.4:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-fold-elimination
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p104-fold-elimination --check-source-history
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B research/p104-fold-elimination/verify.py
```

Both registered normal/optimized checks pass. Direct warning-strict commands take 70.89 s and 71.68 s, each checking 1234 systems, five rejection controls and both complete accepted solver variants. The registered run takes 143.68 s total. Committed bytes, executable modes and declared source-history ancestry pass for all 16 package files at `9a7f206d4e9812d2eec042aed6e40acadacd534d`.

Official export/input integrity passes. Optimized replay with Git absent and all exported files read-only passes in 70.45 s; all 17 exported files retain their bytes and modes.

The package README gives the full timing command and minimal retained-source extraction. RETAINED.json identifies all 50 predecessor files by original Git blob and SHA256 at PR6170 head `445fb9124eb3fcb5d4f342c476b9ae3637f185aa`; the archive is self-contained. No predecessor source is edited.

## Limitations

One shared macOS host and the first H705 fold on the shipped PR6030 word are measured. Solver dimensions are capped at 4096. The retained projection and legality oracle keep their existing scope. Warning-strict controls expose unchanged tkcommon profile-loader ResourceWarnings; these are documented and not suppressed. Full rebuild timing, native/caller/compiler/precision/BIT/outer and formal-kernel checks are unrun. The five selected framework assumptions remain. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Related open work

- #6170 supplies the toolkit and asks for a faster fold pass; this answers one measured first-fold instance through its dominant solver cost.
- #6144 supplies the root/relay descent construction underlying the fold rule; its word and kappa are not new contributions here.
- #6167 changes the later retained-operand word and paid profile; this package changes only construction-time solving.
- #6169 resynthesizes scalar events in another complete P104 word; this package preserves its source fold's complete output rather than claiming a new word.

- #6175 adds exact ADD-coefficient fault localization on an earlier P104 word; this package accelerates a fold solve and computes no repair count.

- #6173 determines joint support in the P104 root code; this solver changes no port geometry.
- #6181 concerns a joint-bank P104 spectral obstruction; this solver changes no Gram operator.
- #6183 concerns contractive P104 mode deletion; this solver preserves the complete output word.
- #6177 accelerates replay planning, a separate command and workload; no performance gains are combined.
- #6179 accelerates task-picker startup, a separate command and workload.
- #6186 accelerates a positive-frame checker, a separate command and workload.

The completion refresh inspected all fifteen other open account PRs created since the advance CLAIM. None supplies a competing fold-solver result or a number for this same complete-fold workload. No extra mathematical computations were run to check other contributions.

## Open next questions

- Does the same substitution help all remaining fold sites and the complete rebuild? Compare every word and acceptance status along that full path.
- Can consecutive Newton systems reuse an exact factorization? First establish a certified relation between those actual matrices.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks passed at exact head `9a7f206d4e9812d2eec042aed6e40acadacd534d` in [run 40886077177](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40886077177). [Plan](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40886077177/job/123490027871) passed in 4m23s; [replay (research/p104-fold-elimination)](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40886077177/job/123492487405) passed in 9m27s. The completed check list was read once and both entries report pass.

Hosted replay certifies the registered normal/optimized conformance checks at this head. It does not independently certify the local performance percentage or supplier admission. All recorded local checks also passed. No code changed after these checks. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review remain unclaimed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** isolated. The new package is opt-in and changes no shared solver or selected frontier.
